how_to_use: This file is a machine-readable map of the Roshera workspace as it stood at git_rev, assembled from five independently verified mapper reports (backend, kernel, frontend, agent-layers, flows). It exists so an agent orchestrating changes can orient quickly without re-deriving structure from scratch. Code is the ultimate truth: this atlas describes one revision and decays from there — re-verify any fact against the current tree before relying on it for a consequential decision, especially module paths, line numbers, and counts.
product_thesis: Roshera is an agent runtime for geometry, not a CAD tool in the traditional sense: the backend/SDK is the product and the React viewport is one thin client among possible clients, with agents (Claude) as the primary orchestrated actor and humans directing at a higher level. The system is built star-topology around a self-certifying B-Rep kernel (geometry-engine) that cannot lie — every mutating operation is checked against a nine-conjunct validity certificate computed fresh from geometry, never asserted, so soundness claims are always re-derived rather than trusted from history. The governing discipline is honest refusal over silent wrong answers: operations outside a verified envelope return typed errors (DisjointDifference, EmptyResult, BlendFailed, quarantine states, Unavailable mass properties) rather than approximations mislabeled as exact. History is event-sourced on a timeline, not a parametric feature tree, and the frontend is backend-driven — no client-side geometry kernel, no client-side mesh generation, sub-element picks are server-resolved.

conjuncts.name: brep_valid

conjuncts.name: watertight
conjuncts.meaning: tessellated mesh has zero boundary edges (manifold_report, chord 0.1, weld 1e-6)

conjuncts.name: manifold
conjuncts.meaning: every mesh edge borders exactly 2 faces

conjuncts.name: oriented
conjuncts.meaning: every directed mesh edge is traversed at most once — catches flipped-normal defects invisible to watertight+manifold alone

conjuncts.name: construction_consistent
conjuncts.meaning: linked source-sketch construction geometry stays co-located within a tolerance-band-expanded bbox (tri-state; only Inconsistent blocks soundness)

conjuncts.name: eyes_consistent
conjuncts.meaning: dual-eye render-free Truth<->Semantic cross-check: every RecognizedFeature must reference a live face and sit on the surface type its label implies; fails closed

conjuncts.name: tessellation.clean
conjuncts.meaning: display-tessellation quality: no degenerate facets, normal agreement >=0.98, analytic agreement >=0.999, zero off-surface facets

conjuncts.name: mesh_quality.clean
conjuncts.meaning: zero boundary-crossing facets and max normal deviation <=40 degrees (aspect-ratio and min-angle are reported, not gated)

carried_not_gating: labels_consistent — tri-state annotation-defect signal; annotation defects are not geometric defects so they don't fail is_sound()
model_debris_orphan_faces — a model-level fact (not this solid's fault), re-scanned on every certificate() call regardless of cache
certificate.computed_at: geometry-engine/src/primitives/topology_builder.rs — BRepModel::certificate (~2642, hot path clones cache under short RwLock read) / compute_certificate (~2687, private, always recomputes from geometry) / certify_solid (~2899, public wrapper)
certificate.memoization: Solid.cached_certificate: RwLock<Option<ValidityCertificate>> (solid.rs ~534). Lock is never held across the heavy compute: short read to check cache, compute lock-free, short write to store; last-write-wins, idempotent recompute.
invalidation_seams: record_operation funnel (topology_builder.rs ~2472): for every RecordedOperation input/output solid, invalidate_certificate() fires before the recorder-forward guard, so it runs even with no recorder attached (e.g. during timeline replay)
SolidStore::get_mut backstop (~1840): invalidates on any mutable borrow of a solid, regardless of call site
certificate.advisory_reconcile: The 14-viewpoint dual-eye reconcile (api-server/src/reconcile_task.rs, VIEWPOINTS=14 at line 51) is advisory-severity and explicitly documented to never affect is_sound(). It runs off the write lock on an owned ModelSnapshot, fire-and-forget, capped at MAX_CONCURRENT_RECONCILES=2. It is distinct from conjunct 7 (eyes_consistent/TruthSemantic), which is synchronous, render-free, and is the one dual-eye axis that does gate the certificate. render/viewpoint.rs (EYE-6, viewpoint-entropy best-view) is a separate on-demand selector, unrelated to the fixed 14.
certificate.mass_properties_provenance: MassPropertiesMethod is Analytical (exact divergence-theorem, planar solids) or Tessellated{rel_tolerance} (Tonon 2004, approx 5e-3 at fine tessellation). Each quantity (volume, center_of_mass, inertia) carries its own Exactness — Exact / Approximate{method, rel_error_bound} / Unavailable — independently, so e.g. volume can be exact while inertia is mesh-estimated. The kernel refuses to fabricate a mass-property number rather than silently degrade its exactness label.

tables: api_keys (FK-free user_id by design — agent keys have no users row)
timeline_events (durability log; FK-free; data JSONB = whole serialized TimelineEvent; sequence_number BIGINT is the replay key; indexed on (session_id, sequence_number))
persistence.durability_model: Append-only event log via api-server/src/durability.rs DatabaseEventSink::persist (one transactional row per TimelineEvent, written by TimelineRecorder's drain worker off the kernel's synchronous path). Boot replay loads all rows for a fixed single-tenant DURABILITY_SESSION_ID = 'roshera-durability-main', ordered by sequence_number, then rebuilds the BRepModel by replaying events (recorder detached during replay — no re-record/re-persist loop). Quarantine: certify_rebuild re-measures soundness from a full trial replay; if a break or corrupt row is found, only the clean prefix (sequence < break) is served, the break is named in logs and via GET /api/durability/status, and the tail is refused rather than silently served.
in_memory_only: uuid_to_local / local_to_uuid ID maps (fresh UUIDs minted every boot)
solid_colors / solid_profiles (re-derived from the durable log at boot; the map itself is volatile)
reconcile caches, request/command/performance metrics, viewport_bridge state
the BRepModel itself — only durability path is a full event replay at boot, there is no snapshot
persistence.durability_off_behavior: ROSHERA_DURABILITY=off (case-insensitive match on 'off') yields a fully volatile scratch server: blank boot (no replay), all persist calls become no-ops, and API-key rehydration is skipped entirely.

auth_model.posture: AuthPosture::Required is the default — an empty environment enforces auth and returns 401 before any handler runs. AuthPosture::InsecureDevBypass activates only via ROSHERA_DEV_INSECURE=1|true, logs a loud warning every boot, and injects a permissive sentinel AuthInfo (also bypasses the 100 req/min rate limit).
schemes: Both schemes are validated through the single session-manager AuthManager
auth_model.key_lifecycle: provision_api_key_handler (auth.rs:471) writes through AuthManager::provision_api_key; list (570) and revoke (605) are separate handlers. Keys are rehydrated from the durable api_keys table at boot (gated on durability_enabled) via attach_api_key_store + load_persisted_api_keys, so keys and their revoked state survive a restart. There is no provisioning HTTP route beyond these handlers and no self-service revocation endpoint documented for agents.
auth_model.ws_auth: in-band Authenticate frame — the WS upgrade itself is exempt (browsers cannot set upgrade headers), so the client must send {type:'Authenticate', token} as its first message after onopen; the command surface is gated per-connection on that frame, not on the upgrade request

record_operation forwards to TimelineRecorder::record, a non-blocking try_send into a bounded 16,384-slot MPSC channel; a background tokio worker drains it FIFO into Timeline::add_operation, minting a sequence_number and appending a TimelineEvent
the same drain worker calls DatabaseEventSink::persist (off the kernel's sync path) to append the event as a Postgres row keyed on DURABILITY_SESSION_ID
returns {success, solid_id, perception, object, stats}; the MCP tool returns {object_uuid, part_id, placement}

broadcast_object_created sends an ObjectCreated frame on the process-wide broadcaster to every /ws client; ws-bridge queues the upsert into the scene store for CADViewport (dual-eye reconcile fires separately, async, never blocking this response)
certify_solid wraps certificate(): hot path clones the RwLock-cached certificate; cold path calls compute_certificate and stores the result (last-write-wins, lock never held across compute)
invalidation fires from three seams: the record_operation funnel over inputs/outputs, set_solid_construction, and the SolidStore::get_mut backstop on any mutable borrow

certified_response spawns reconcile_task::spawn_reconcile fire-and-forget: a brief read lock takes a ModelSnapshot, drops the guard, renders 14 Fibonacci-sphere viewpoints, and runs reconcile_full (truth cert vs scene render vs semantic features), caching by (solid_id, perception_fingerprint) under a 2-way concurrency semaphore — never blocks the mutation response

rebuild_certificate::certify_rebuild produces a RebuildCertificate with per-feature FeatureStatus (Rebuilt/Unaffected/Failed/Dangling/Blocked/Stale) and a re-measured, never-asserted global is_sound, rooted at the earliest active mould target

EventCertificate is defined (from_solid_certificate/skipped_solid/for_sketch/for_assembly + store_in) but has no production producer: store_in is called exactly once, from the module's own #[cfg(test)]; the only production consumer, from_metadata, always reads None, so every real evidence-pack event carries a null certificate plus certificate_absent_reason
builds a fresh BRepModel, then constructs DatabaseConfig{PostgreSQL, run_migrations:true} and connects via PostgresDatabase::new
'migrations' means inline CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements in run_migrations(), not sqlx::migrate!

boot_replay: ROSHERA_DURABILITY=off -> Disabled (blank boot); else restore branch metadata, load all timeline events, empty -> Empty; deserialize rows tracking the earliest corrupt row; certify_rebuild finds the first replay break

quarantine boundary = min(first replay break, first corrupt row); if present, only the clean prefix (sequence < boundary) is served as Quarantined{...}, logged as an error and never hidden; otherwise Active{events_replayed}. Chosen events rehydrate with original ids/sequences, the recorder stays detached during replay (no re-record/re-persist), and a fresh UUID is minted per restored solid
GET /api/durability/status reports {session_id, durability_enabled, quarantined, status} — quarantine is always surfaced, never hidden
API key rehydration (gated on durability_enabled): attach_api_key_store + load_persisted_api_keys restores real active/revoked flags
register: username validated (>=3 alnum/_/-), user_id = 'user_{username}', duplicate check, Argon2 hash_password + complexity check, save_user
login: load UserData, is_active check, Argon2 verify_password, create_token (SessionToken with embedded JWT refresh) returns {token, refresh_token, expires_in, permissions}

builds operations[] (sequence, event_id, op_kind, params verbatim, timestamp, author, author_kind, certificate = EventCertificate::from_metadata), final_state.parts[] (mass properties per live solid, provenance-labeled), notebook (blackboard snapshot verbatim), recomputed (separately labeled EvidenceRecompute from certify_rebuild), and a manifest (generated_at, kernel_version, scope, operation_count, durability status)

honesty rules are enforced in code: an absent certificate is null plus certificate_absent_reason (never fabricated — and today fires on every real event per the EventCertificate gap); a degenerate solid gets null mass_properties plus a reason; the recompute note literally reads 'Re-measured NOW ... NOT recorded history'; quarantine state is always surfaced via manifest.durability, never omitted
run.mjs preflights /health, loads the 17-scenario index, runs the suite, prints a scorecard, clears parts, writes report.json; exit code equals the number of failed scenarios
lib/client.mjs is a thin HTTP client sending X-Roshera-Agent: AgentEvalAlpha over the same REST surface roshera-mcp uses — straight REST, not through the MCP protocol
each scenario exports {id, title, dims, budgetMs, run(ctx, t)} where ctx = {c, time, geom} and t = Checks

four scoring dimensions: correctness (analytic/structural oracles), soundness (t.sound asserts perception.sound===true against CERT_DIMS), honesty (t.unsound asserts the kernel correctly refused, e.g. the saddle canary scenario 08), performance (budgetMs wall-clock)
make_drawing -> POST /api/parts/{part_id}/drawing?name=

create_part_drawing(_by_uuid) -> create_part_drawing_inner -> build_standard_drawing_off_lock: a brief read lock takes a ModelSnapshot, drops the guard, then the heavy build runs on spawn_blocking off the lock

standard_drawing_auto builds pass 1 (unit-scale extents for Front/Top/Right/Iso, pick_sheet + layout_four_view) then pass 2 per projection (HLR visibility, dimensions, centerlines), dedups dimensions globally per ISO-129, attaches the hole table, attaches SECTION A-A when bore sites exist, attaches GD&T annotations and ISO-286-style tolerances, and places the pictorial isometric last via free-space search

verify_drawing runs a quality check, the drawing is inserted into state.drawings, and a drawing.create_from_part timeline event is recorded with the source solid as input so the sheet is downstream in the feature DAG (mould marks it dirty and re-derives)
drawing_export_sheet -> GET /api/drawings/{id}/pdf -> export_pdf -> render_drawing_pdf returns bytes; dxf/svg are symmetric

a separate certified-readback surface (drawing_read_semantics/drawing_query -> /semantic, /query) re-certifies against the LIVE model via certify_off_lock and honestly refuses render_only or unprovenanced content
create, add_instance, list_instances, transform_instance, mate, solve, certify, dof, drag, interference, view, plus a one-shot assembly_verify
create_assembly / add_instance write true-assembly instances that reference shared kernel geometry by part_id/transform — no boolean merge
create_mate writes the assembly doc under the model+doc write lock, then records the op_mate_add event after dropping the locks
solve -> solve_core -> Assembly::solve(): rigid-body blocks + mate/driven-joint index set, analytic screw-calculus Jacobian, gauss_newton iterates g->0; success records op_solve with poses

certify: prepare_certify resolves connectors and tessellates under locks, then the heavy certificate (mates-consistent, fully-grounded, DOF/mobility, static interference, swept clearance) runs off the locks on an owned snapshot — the same off-lock discipline as reconcile

static interference uses Parry TriMesh per instance local frame with exact EPA penetration depth on convex-hull/VHACD pieces; swept interference derives mechanisms/joints from mates and certifies continuous clearance via Parry nonlinear TOI (Rapier CCD machinery) between exact screw motions, producing first_contact and min_certified_clearance
view -> view_assembly composes one PNG per instance (part_id -> kernel solid + transform + color) via render::render_instances_dir — geometry is referenced per-instance, never merged

known_gaps_and_stale.evidence: timeline-engine/src/event_certificate.rs defines store_in(metadata); grepping the whole roshera-backend workspace shows store_in( is called exactly once, from the module's own #[cfg(test)] (event_certificate.rs:407). The only production consumer is the read-side from_metadata.
known_gaps_and_stale.implication: Every real evidence-pack event's certificate field reads None and is served as null plus a certificate_absent_reason — evidence packs today carry no per-operation certificates for real activity, only for the module's own test.

known_gaps_and_stale.finding: timeline-engine's storage/ StorageEngine is dead code
known_gaps_and_stale.evidence: A file-based StorageEngine (event_log/index/snapshot) is defined in timeline-engine/src/storage but grep-confirmed never referenced outside its own mod.rs.
known_gaps_and_stale.implication: Live persistence is entirely api-server/src/durability.rs (DatabaseEventSink) + session-manager::database — the storage/ module is inert and should not be assumed to be the durability path.

known_gaps_and_stale.finding: Backend CLAUDE.md says 7 crates; the tree has 10
known_gaps_and_stale.evidence: roshera-backend/Cargo.toml workspace members list 10 crates including ros-format, verdict-harness, and assembly-engine, which the backend-local CLAUDE.md does not mention.
known_gaps_and_stale.implication: The backend-local documentation is stale relative to the actual workspace shape; don't trust its crate inventory without checking Cargo.toml.

known_gaps_and_stale.finding: enforce_permission_layer's doc-comment describes a removed toggle
known_gaps_and_stale.evidence: The doc-comment on api-server's enforce_permission_layer still describes the ROSHERA_REQUIRE_AUTH soft/strict toggle; the code no longer reads that variable — scope checks (require_create/modify/export_geometry) are unconditional today.
known_gaps_and_stale.implication: Anyone reading only the comment will believe permission enforcement is configurable when it is not; the doc needs to be corrected to match current unconditional behavior.

known_gaps_and_stale.evidence: Repo-root .mcp.json configures the roshera MCP server with env ROSHERA_URL=http://localhost:8081 and no ROSHERA_API_KEY.
known_gaps_and_stale.implication: This configuration only functions against a backend running with ROSHERA_DEV_INSECURE=1 — it is a dev-insecure assumption baked into the checked-in MCP config, not something that works against a Required-posture backend.

known_gaps_and_stale.finding: assembly-engine is fully standalone (zero workspace deps)
known_gaps_and_stale.evidence: grep-confirmed: assembly-engine's Cargo.toml pulls in only parry3d-f64 + serde, no intra-workspace crate dependencies, even though api-server depends on it.
known_gaps_and_stale.implication: This is an observation, not a defect — assembly-engine is architecturally decoupled from the rest of the kernel/timeline stack and could in principle be extracted or reused independently.

known_gaps_and_stale.finding: Boot replay mints fresh UUIDs — identity is not preserved across a restart
known_gaps_and_stale.evidence: durability.rs boot_replay rehydrates events with their original ids/sequences into the timeline, but register_id_mapping mints a brand-new UUID per restored solid rather than reusing the pre-restart UUID.
known_gaps_and_stale.implication: Any external reference to a solid's UUID from before a restart (e.g. a client-held object_uuid) is invalidated by a restart. Documented as in-scope for Slice 1 durability, not yet closed.

known_gaps_and_stale.finding: No durability snapshots — every boot is a full event replay
known_gaps_and_stale.evidence: durability.rs has no snapshot mechanism; boot_replay always replays the entire timeline_events table for DURABILITY_SESSION_ID from scratch.
known_gaps_and_stale.implication: Boot time scales with total history size; this is documented as acceptable for the current alpha stage but will need snapshotting before history grows large.

known_gaps_and_stale.finding: Chamfer on closed (rim/seam) edges only supports the Plane-Cylinder face pair
known_gaps_and_stale.evidence: geometry-engine/src/operations/chamfer.rs:1118-1123 (chamfer_distances_for_closed_edge): if both adjacent faces are cylinders, or neither is, the function returns OperationError::NotImplemented('Closed-edge chamfer ... currently supports only a Plane-Cylinder pair in this slice'); the open-edge chamfer path is unaffected.
known_gaps_and_stale.implication: Chamfering a closed rim edge between two non-plane-cylinder face kinds (e.g. cone-cylinder, cylinder-cylinder, or a rim entirely between curved faces) is refused today rather than attempted — a scoped gap, not a silent wrong answer.

glossary.certificate: ValidityCertificate — a nine-conjunct, geometry-derived soundness verdict recomputed on demand (never asserted from history) for every solid; is_sound() requires all nine conjuncts to hold, with two further fields (labels_consistent, model_debris_orphan_faces) carried but not gating.
glossary.perception line: The compact sound/brep_valid/watertight/manifold/oriented/self_intersection_free/verdict/cert summary embedded in every mutating-operation response so an agent gets the certificate inline, without a follow-up call.
glossary.dual-eye reconcile: A cross-check between the kernel's own geometric Truth, a rendered Scene, and the labeled Semantic feature set, run along four axes (TruthScene, Coverage, TruthSemantic, SceneSemantic); only TruthSemantic (conjunct 7, eyes_consistent) is synchronous and gates the certificate — the other axes drive the 14-viewpoint async reconcile, which is advisory-only.
glossary.typed refusal: The kernel's discipline of returning a specific, named error (e.g. DisjointDifference, EmptyResult, BlendFailed, Unavailable mass property, Quarantined durability state) rather than a generic failure or a silently-approximated answer, whenever an operation falls outside its verified envelope.
glossary.ratchet / KNOWN_REDS: KNOWN_REDS.md is a machine-readable allowlist of pre-existing failing tests; entries may only be removed once a test goes green and may never be added without an accompanying diagnosis doc — the allowlist is currently empty.
glossary.red-gate: roshera-backend/scripts/red-gate.ps1 — the required pre-merge CI gate that runs the geometry-engine test suite and diffs the result against KNOWN_REDS.md, exiting non-zero on any new or ratchet-violating red.
glossary.timeline mould: The mould mechanism (timeline-engine/src/mould) lets a parameter on a past event be overridden; incremental.rs then does a dirty-subtree rebuild of only the downstream-affected parts of the model rather than replaying the whole timeline from scratch.
glossary.quarantine: The durability state entered when boot_replay finds a corrupt or broken event row: only the clean prefix of history is served, the break point is named in logs and via /api/durability/status, and the remainder is refused rather than silently dropped or served anyway.
glossary.workbench / bench: roshera-mcp's mechanism for toggling groups of related MCP tool handles on/off (sketch, assembly, drawing, analysis, labels) to keep the live tool surface within an attention budget (LIVE_SURFACE_CEILING=35); it is never a capability gate because every tool remains reachable through invoke.
glossary.meta-funnel: The three always-on MCP meta-tools (find_tool, describe_tool, invoke) that let an agent discover and call any tool in the full registry — including ones not currently enabled as direct handles — through the identical validation and dispatch path a direct call would use.
glossary.evidence pack: GET /api/evidence-pack — a single authenticated response bundling recorded operations with their certificates-as-recorded, final mass properties, and the blackboard notebook, plus a separately-labeled live recompute, so an agent or auditor can see both what was claimed at the time and what re-measurement says now.
glossary.blackboard: A backend-persisted, scope-partitioned (document / part:<uuid> / assembly:<uuid>) shared notebook of text entries that both humans and agents read and write, with an append-only Add/Edit/Delete event log underneath each scope's current line state.
glossary.readable surface: geometry-engine/src/readable — the module the mapper reports describe as 'the pillar that makes Roshera an agent runtime for geometry': wire records, dimensioning, feature extraction, and blackboard-claim verification exposed thinly through api-server's /api/agent/* handlers.
glossary.persistent id: A topological entity identifier intended to survive across operations/rebuilds (not just within a single BRepModel instance) so downstream references (labels, moulds, drawings) keep pointing at 'the same' face/edge across history; landed for some paths, not yet universal (fillet/chamfer/pattern don't mint persistent-id lineage in all cases).
glossary.bounded_exec: api-server's mechanism (Task #41) for running a heavy kernel operation on a deep-cloned model inside spawn_blocking under a per-operation-class wall-clock time budget, off the write lock, only swapping the mutated clone back under a brief write guard on success.
